bullets.title: Tech-led selloff: semis tank on Samsung miss, DeepSeek chip threat, momentum unwind
bullets.body: US equities closed lower (S&P -0.45%, Nasdaq -1.16%, Russell -0.90%) as Samsung's Q2 revenue miss triggered a global semi selloff and China's DeepSeek announcing its own AI chip development weighed on the sector. Price momentum factor (CIISPMUT) fell 6.6% w/w — 2nd worst 5-day drawdown since 2004 — as the long semis/short software trade violently unwound; the S&P gained 0.1% during the move, consistent with ~60% of historical momentum drawdowns where broader market doesn't follow.

bullets.title: Momentum factor: further Price Mo weakness likely, but not a broad market sell signal
bullets.body: Price Momentum is down 17.4% from peak with vol at the 97th percentile, a level unmatched outside recessions since 2005. Historically, sharp drawdowns predict further Price Mo underperformance but better-than-normal S&P 500 forward returns, especially in non-recession periods. EPS Momentum is only down 1.8%, remaining durable; the long EPS Mo / short Price Mo factor (MS22EVPM) gained 5.4% YTD.

bullets.title: AI capex 'air pocket': demand arriving in separate waves, market demanded synchronized adoption
bullets.body: A detailed note flags that AI demand is splitting into three curves — coding inference (accelerating), enterprise AI (constrained by governance), and consumer personal assistants (slower than expected) — after Meta acknowledged agentic AI progress is lagging and is now building a cloud business to resell excess compute. Microsoft is replacing OpenAI and Anthropic with in-house models in Excel/Outlook, reinforcing fears of frontier model commoditization. Market is shifting from rewarding AI capex by default to demanding clarity on ROI and revenue conversion timelines.

bullets.title: Iran tanker strikes spike WTI +5%; US revokes Iranian crude sales licenses
bullets.body: Iran struck three commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz; the US subsequently revoked waivers authorizing Iranian crude oil sales, sending WTI crude up ~5% to ~$72. The oil spike drove energy outperformance on the day (energy among the top SPX sectors) and contributed to Treasury yield pressure alongside hawkish Fed commentary.

bullets.title: 10Y yields +8bps to 4.55%; Williams hawkish, JPM sees auction needing more concession
bullets.body: Treasury yields rose 4-8bps across the curve, driven by Iran escalation and hawkish comments from Fed President Williams. JPM previews the $39B 10-year auction (July 8) with caution, noting 10-year yields appear ~20bp rich on fundamentals and that the June auction's strong end-user demand (90.5%) and investment manager surge (+3.5%-pts to 74.3%) may not repeat. JPM maintains short 10Y Treasuries vs German bunds; tactical support seen at 4.56-4.58%.

bullets.title: Fed inflation expectations rising: 1Y to 3.7% (highest since Sep-23), 3Y to 3.3% (highest since Jun-22)
bullets.body: The Fed's 1-year inflation expectations rose to 3.7% — the highest since September 2023 — while 3-year expectations hit 3.3%, the highest since June 2022. A separate note argues the Fed's Phillips Curve framework oversimplifies inflation drivers and that forward guidance away from the zero lower bound offers only disadvantages, citing the 2021-22 experience as proof.

bullets.title: MS credit desk: sell credit vol, buy equity vol — RV opportunity as credit stays too calm
bullets.body: Realized credit vol is muted at 0.39 IG bps/day over the past two weeks while equity vol is being driven by AI and tech. MS favors outright credit payers and payer spreads given low-premium environment, with funding backdrop benign (HYG revcon-implied at -40). iBoxx flows quiet with modest IG/LQD buying; opportunistic sellers in loan TRS on compressing NAV discounts.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex accelerating: Amazon raises $25B in bonds, 2026 industry spend tracking $750B+
bullets.body: Amazon launched a $25B eight-part bond sale — its largest ever — in support of $200B guided 2026 capex (vs. $131B in 2025), with hyperscaler industry capex expected to hit $750B+, up ~85% YoY. The bond sale itself pressured existing hyperscaler debt as traders sold securities to fund purchases. JPM maintains a tactically bullish call citing strong corporate balance sheets and earnings estimate increases.

bullets.title: Renewables sector -6-9% on hydrogen/solar reversal; natural gas utilities lead; EIA forecasts record gas demand in 2027
bullets.body: Power & utilities saw sharp sector rotation: OKLO -7.7%, BE -8.7%, SMR -6.9%, NNE -6.5%, GEV -6.5% as hydrogen and solar reversed prior day gains. IPPs TLN and NRG among key losers. Natural gas utilities bucked the trend, up +2.2% on the S&P 1500 sub-index, supported by EIA forecasting US electric power sector natural gas consumption will set a record in 2027 (+3%).

bullets.title: Real estate outperforms (+1.6%); data center REITs +25.7% YTD on AI warehouse demand
bullets.body: S&P 500 Real Estate index gained 1.6% vs. S&P -0.45%, led by data center REITs (+1.75% daily, +25.68% YTD) on continued AI-driven warehouse demand, with Meta and Google leasing ~4MSF in 2026 and JLL projecting 14MSF by 2030. Healthcare REITs also gained +1.74% as Barclays initiated senior housing bullishly (AHR OW, $61 PT). Office REITs declined -1.67% on MetroLoft collapse risk; 10Y yield +8bps to 4.55% and 30Y mortgage +4bps to 6.63%.

bullets.title: US hotel RevPAR +10.8% YoY week of July 4; luxury +24.4% on World Cup boost
bullets.body: Total US RevPAR accelerated to +10.8% YoY (vs +9.7% prior week) with luxury chain segment at +24.4% driven by World Cup hosting cities. July 4 itself was +27% with higher-than-usual visitor turnout, offsetting double-digit declines in the days leading up to the holiday. Economy segment lagged at +2.7%, with its two-year stack decelerating 330bps.

bullets.title: Citi credit card data: US retail spending accelerating; June +1.4%, 2Q running +1.3% vs. 1Q -0.4%
bullets.body: Citi's credit card tracker shows June overall spending at +1.4% (+1.8% ex-food), a slight acceleration from May's +1.2%, with 2QTD running +1.3% vs. 1Q's -0.4% contraction. Jewelry surged 1,630bps to +24.7% and off-price retailers accelerated 420bps to +12.1%, while apparel decelerated 410bps to -10.7%. No sub-category data signals an overall spending slowdown.

bullets.title: Bank deposit costs rising: CD rates +8bps in June, competitive cycle early-stage with 57 markets at risk
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley flags highest average CD rates rose 8bps in June to 3.74%, driven by forward curve repricing and accelerating 7.4% YoY loan growth. 13 of 35 tracked banks raised CD rates in June vs. only 3 that lowered. MS identifies 57 markets with large-bank expansion plans, characterizing this as the early stage of a multi-year competitive deposit cycle.

bullets.title: Samsung Q2 revenue miss (-0.7% vs. consensus) triggers memory sector selloff despite year-to-date massive runs
bullets.body: Samsung's Q2 preliminary revenue of KRW171T missed by 0.7% (operating profit beat +2.0%), triggering sharp declines in MU, SNDK, STX, and WDC — all of which are still up 200-575% YTD. A new $517.9B chip ecosystem capex announcement from Samsung and SK Hynix for two new Korean fab sites compounded supply concerns, even as Counterpoint Research reports memory prices for consumer, mobile, server, and PC products continue to rise.

bullets.title: NVDA framed as 'Central Bank of AI' via neocloud backstop; $7T debt expected in AI financing by 2029
bullets.body: JPM describes NVDA's role in backstopping neocloud financing agreements as akin to a 'Central Bank of AI,' with $7T in AI-related debt expected to be outstanding by 2029. Semis valuations remain elevated while Mag 7 is trading near trough levels vs. SPX — JPM frames this as a potential opportunity to buy Mag 7 into weakness. AI Vulnerable basket (ACN, services) also outperforming amid internal tech rotation.

bullets.title: SpaceX-Tesla combination: strategically coherent but regulatory and governance hurdles are gating items
bullets.body: JPM lays out four potential deal structures for a SPCX-TSLA combination, with all-stock SPCX-led acquisition viewed as most likely given SPCX's $2.2T market cap vs. TSLA's $1.4T and Musk's ~85% SPCX voting control vs. ~20% at TSLA. Key risks: SPCX's government contracts plus TSLA's China manufacturing creates national security tensions, and antitrust scrutiny is expected. TSLA fundamentals are described as turning the corner on strong 2Q deliveries and FSD momentum.

bullets.title: Asia defense spending accelerating to $700B in 2026, targeting $1-1.2T medium-term — capex supercycle forming
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley estimates Asia defense spending reached $700B in 2026 with a CAGR that accelerated to 6.6% over 2022-26 from 4.5% over 2012-22, as policymakers target $1-1.2T medium-term. The report flags the drag on productivity will be partially offset by AI and innovation spillovers from defense investment; DM Asia and China face lower fiscal strain vs. EM Asia peers.

bullets.title: Banks in talks to acquire Fiserv debit network to bypass federal fee limits — potential V/MA headwind
bullets.body: A consortium including JPM, BAC, WFC, and PNC is in preliminary talks to acquire Fiserv's payments network to circumvent federal debit-card fee limits, which would be a structural headwind for Visa and Mastercard. Separately, UBS expects Q2 bank earnings to show 'beats' from capital markets/trading and 'misses' from deposit costs; investment banking revenues from GSIBs expected up meaningfully YoY.

bullets.title: QQQ puts recommended as best hedge to momentum/sentiment risk; MTUM ETF hedges favored over index
bullets.body: Citi recommends QQQ puts as the cleanest hedge to current sentiment and positioning risks, with semis congestion (CIEQCSX1) as a low-carry complement. A separate derivatives note favors hedging via MTUM ETF and names targeting DRAM exposure over traditional index hedges, with XHB August puts flagged as attractive after housing's rally off May lows. Levered ETF AUM (SOXL) sits at midpoint of its $10-35B range — positioning risk present but described as contained.

bullets.title: Buyback blackout near peak with ~93% of S&P 500 companies in blackout ahead of Q2 earnings
bullets.body: Approximately 93% of S&P 500 companies are currently in buyback blackout periods heading into Q2 earnings season, removing a key technical bid from the market. YTD 2026 buyback authorizations of $963B remain ahead of 2025's $833B pace, suggesting the technical support will return post-earnings.
